paths.description: Primary accommodation-search landing page and booking-entry state; exercised tabs, empty search, preferences, mobile reflow, performance, security and memory.
London destination/detail-listing archetype representing discovery after a search.
Promotional/listing archetype representing coupon and offer browsing.
Editorial/content archetype linked from primary navigation; capture returned a bare 403.

findings.summary: The booking experience remains light-only when the user requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: The light and dark-condition mobile screenshots are pixel-equivalent in their white surfaces; the preference probe reports colorScheme "normal".
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, border, and control tokens.

findings.summary: Core accommodation pages render a desktop-width canvas inside a 360px mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: Home and London layout captures report 1,132px scroll width and 772px horizontal overflow at 360px; screenshots show controls and headings clipped off-screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed/minimum desktop widths, preserve a device-width viewport, and use intrinsic/fluid layouts that reflow search controls and cards.

findings.summary: The London listing has severe layout instability during load.
findings.evidence: The 360px layout observer measured CLS 0.570, dominated by a single 0.57 shift; the deals page also measured 0.117.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions for asynchronously inserted search/calendar, hero, and promotional regions and avoid late state replacement above the fold.

findings.summary: Mobile load and interactivity are slow and main-thread heavy.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.3s, TBT 770ms, TTI 17.4s and performance 50; the independent trace found a 279ms long task and 259ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the critical booking path, split and defer non-critical work, break long tasks, and prioritize only LCP-critical resources.

findings.summary: The homepage ships excessive JavaScript and unused front-end code.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 2.66MB of script transfer and a 1.36MB bundle; Lighthouse estimates 889KiB unused JavaScript, 75KiB unused CSS, and 2.6s JS execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split the homepage, remove duplicate/legacy bundles, and defer search, account, promotion, and recommendation code until needed.

findings.summary: Promotional imagery is oversized and mostly served in legacy formats.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 35 legacy-format images, five oversized images, five without srcset, and 40 without dimensions; HAR transferred 2.29MB of images including a 1.14MB banner.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive AVIF/WebP sources for campaign art, size them to rendered slots, and include intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: The homepage fails multiple automated accessibility fundamentals.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility score was 86 with failures for colour contrast, missing image alt text, visible-label/name mismatch, and restricted viewport scaling.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix each Lighthouse/axe node: raise colour contrast, supply meaningful alt text, align accessible names with visible labels, and permit zoom.

findings.summary: Important browser security policies are missing and cookies are overly permissive.
findings.evidence: Headers probe found no CSP, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Cookie audit found eight flagged cookies, including two without Secure and pervasive SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive nonce/hash CSP, explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and narrow cookie Secure/SameSite attributes to actual cross-site needs.

findings.summary: The cookie preference panel obscures content and is not exposed as a semantic dialog/popover.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot shows the panel covering roughly the lower quarter of the booking form; DOM probe found zero dialog, role=dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an appropriate dialog/popover primitive with labelled semantics, focus handling, light-dismiss where appropriate, and a compact non-obscuring layout.

findings.summary: Submitting the empty destination state gives no visible recovery guidance.
findings.evidence: After activating SEARCH with an empty destination, the captured page shows no validation message, invalid styling, or focus cue; the text input is not marked required.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark the destination requirement semantically, validate after interaction, focus the invalid field, and announce a concise actionable error.

findings.summary: The date overlay does not fit or reposition within the mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: The 360px London screenshot shows the calendar panel and its content cut off at the right edge while the page itself is 1,132px wide.
findings.suggestedFix: Anchor the calendar to its trigger with collision-aware fallback positions and provide a true full-width mobile presentation.

findings.summary: Core content is invisible to clients that do not execute JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetch returned HTTP 200 and 195KB raw HTML but zero content text, 0% rendered-word coverage, no raw title/H1/description, and a blank crawler screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the core offer, headings, search form and destination links, then hydrate enhancements without replacing usable HTML.

findings.summary: The page uses a deprecated API and omits source maps for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices score was 81 with one deprecation warning and failed valid-source-maps audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the deprecated API call and publish production source maps to the configured secure debugging endpoint.

findings.summary: Important links lack descriptive accessible text.
findings.evidence: The London DOM probe counted 53 links with no visible/accessible text; Lighthouse also failed descriptive link text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every crawlable card and icon link descriptive text or an accessible name that communicates its destination.

findings.summary: A linked content archetype fails as a bare 403 page with no recovery path.
findings.evidence: The travel-guide mobile capture consists only of “403 Forbidden”, without navigation, explanation, retry, or link back; homepage HAR also logged six 502 and two 403 API responses.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a branded, accessible failure state with retry/home options and prevent transient API failures from degrading the surrounding shell.

findings.summary: The initial homepage memory footprint is large for a search landing page.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contained 1,211,314 nodes, 4,964,920 edges and 66.1MB self size before a booking flow was started.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile retained objects and component trees, avoid eagerly mounting below-fold/promotional systems, and lazy-initialize non-critical features.

findings.summary: The commerce workflow is not reliably machine-readable to non-JavaScript agents.
findings.evidence: The non-JS crawler receives 0% content coverage and blank core content; no structured agent capability was found in the rendered probes.
findings.suggestedFix: First expose server-rendered semantic booking controls, then provide narrowly scoped, confirmable agent tools for search and itinerary actions.
